metadata.note: Verbatim DDInter 2.0 slice for issue #250's remaining family — the influenza A/Vietnam antigen, whose row canonicalRow elected by MISREADING a trailing parenthetical. The shipped KB files both rows under the substance name 'Influenza A virus A/Vietnam/1194/2004 (H5N1) antigen (formaldehyde inactivated)'. DDInter2155 carries a display name with a dropped leading 'I' and no drugbank_id, so DdiDrugReferenceSource files it under the same substance; it is listed FIRST here, exactly as in the shipped file, because that is what the defect turns on. Its name carries no TRAILING parenthetical — '(h5n1)' sits mid-name and TRAILING_QUALIFIER is end-anchored — so namesNoRoute() called it unqualified, while the correctly-spelled DDInter925, whose display name IS its own substanceName, was called route-qualified and lost rung one. Ozanimod is the one partner of that family whose RENDERED note differs between the two rows, which is why it is the partner here: the typo row's note stops at 'a diminished or suboptimal immunologic response' while the correctly-spelled row's adds 'Vaccination may be less effective during and for up to three months after discontinuation of ozanimod therapy'. So one chip shows both halves of the change — canonicalRow picking the name, and outranks, freed of the same misreading, no longer crediting the typo row's shorter note. Taken unedited from the shipped 19 MB KB (rows DDInter2155, DDInter925, DDInter1376 and their two interaction rows with their mechanisms); the typo itself is left as loaded, which is issue #196's upstream handoff.

7456.text: The administration of inactivated, killed, or otherwise noninfectious vaccines during ozanimod therapy is generally safe but may be associated with a diminished or suboptimal immunologic response.

2742.text: INTERVAL: The administration of inactivated, killed, or otherwise noninfectious vaccines during ozanimod therapy is generally safe but may be associated with a diminished or suboptimal immunologic response. Vaccination may be less effective during and for up to three months after discontinuation of ozanimod therapy.
